text: The 2021–22 season marked the 120th season in the history of Brighton & Hove Albion and their fifth consecutive year in the top flight of English football. The club competed in the Premier League, the FA Cup, and the EFL Cup, exiting both cup competitions in the fourth round. Brighton finished ninth in the league, their highest-ever top-flight finish, surpassing their previous best of 13th place from the 1981–82 season. The season began with three pre-season friendlies: a goalless draw against Rangers at Ibrox on 24 July, featuring former Albion player Connor Goldson; a 3–1 win over Luton Town a week later, with goals from Aaron Connolly, Enock Mwepu, and Percy Tau, managed by former Seagulls player and coach Nathan Jones; and a 2–0 home defeat to La Liga side Getafe on 7 August, following the return of key players like captain Lewis Dunk and Leandro Trossard. Brighton opened the league campaign with a 2–1 victory over Burnley, with goals from Neal Maupay and Alexis Mac Allister, and followed it with a 2–0 win against Watford on 21 August, marking their best start in a top-flight campaign and their first match in front of a full stadium since March 2020. In the EFL Cup second round, they defeated Cardiff City 2–0, with Jakub Moder and Andi Zeqiri scoring their first goals for the club. Their first league loss came on 28 August, a 2–0 home defeat to Everton, with Taylor Richards making his league and Premier League debut. In a first derby match against Crystal Palace on 27 September, Brighton were behind after Trossard conceded a penalty scored by Wilfried Zaha, but Joël Veltman's long ball led to Neal Maupay scoring a 90+5th-minute equalizer. A second league loss occurred on 23 October, a 4–1 home defeat to Manchester City, with the City side scoring their first three goals in 18 minutes. In the EFL Cup fourth round, they lost to Leicester City on penalties after a 2–2 draw, with Mwepu scoring his first goal for the club and Jürgen Locadia making his first start and only second appearance in over two years. On 24 October, Brighton drew 2–2 with Liverpool after coming from 2–0 down, with Mwepu scoring his first league goal. On 20 November, manager Alex Potter made his 100th appearance in charge with a 2–0 away loss to Aston Villa. On 6 December, Brighton were drawn away to West Bromwich Albion in the third round of the FA Cup, to be played on 8 January 2022. Their fixture against Tottenham Hotspur on 12 December was postponed due to high COVID-19 cases in the Spurs squad. Brighton played a 1–0 home loss against Wolves on 15 December, with several absences due to injury, suspension, and COVID-19, and their match against Manchester United on 18 December was also postponed two days before kickoff due to cases in both squads. After a 12-game winless run starting on 19 September, Brighton beat Brentford 2–0 on Boxing Day, moving into the top half of the table and securing a double over the Bees after a prior away win in September. In the FA Cup third round on 8 January, Brighton won 2–1 after extra time against West Brom, with Odel Offiah making his first start and Kjell Scherpen making his debut as goalkeeper. In the reverse fixture against Palace on 15 January, Pascal Groß's penalty was saved by Jack Butland, Maupay's goal was disallowed for a high boot, and Joachim Andersen scored an own goal in the 87th minute after a low-paced pass from Maupay. Brighton were knocked out of the FA Cup in the fourth round on 5 February, losing 3–1 to Tottenham after a Harry Kane double and a Solly March own goal, with Yves Bissouma providing a brief hope before Kane scored his second. Their record-breaking seven-match unbeaten run ended on 15 February in Potter's 100th league match, with a 2–0 away loss to Manchester United at Old Trafford, after Dunk was sent off for denying Anthony Elanga a run on goal—initially shown a yellow card, but VAR reviewed and deemed it a sending-off. After six consecutive defeats, Brighton drew 0–0 with Norwich City on 2 April, with Maupay's penalty narrowly missing the target. A week later, on 9 April, they defeated Arsenal 2–1, with Mwepu scoring and assisting on his first start since a long injury absence, and Moisés Caicedo making his Premier League debut and assisting Mwepu's goal. Seven days later, on 16 April, Trossard scored two goals in consecutive games, including a 90th-minute goal, helping Brighton go six games unbeaten in the capital. On 30 April, Brighton beat Wolves 3–0 at Molineux, reaching 44 points—breaking their previous record of 41—and winning 10 league matches, surpassing their previous record of nine. On 7 May, Brighton defeated Manchester United 4–0 at the AMEX, their biggest ever top-flight result and first home win of 2022, in front of a record crowd of 31,637. Moisés Caicedo and Marc Cucurella scored their first goals for the club, Pascal Groß scored his first of the season, and Trossard scored one and assisted two others, ending Brighton's hopes for UEFA Champions League qualification in the 2022–23 season. At the end-of-season awards, Marc Cucurella won both Players' Player and Player of the Season, Jeremy Sarmiento won Young Player of the Season, Enock Mwepu won The Seagulls Goal of the Season for his 20-yard strike against Liverpool in October. Brighton finished ninth after beating West Ham 3–1 in the final match, with Joël Veltman scoring his second goal for the club. The victory brought their points total to 51, 10 points above their previous record, and 42 goals—the most in a Premier League season. This was also the first time since joining the Premier League that Brighton finished ahead of rivals Crystal Palace, who finished 12th. Pre-season fixtures included matches against Rangers, Luton Town, and Getafe. Key player movements included Florin Andone joining Cádiz on a season-long loan on 23 August, Percy Tau joining Al Ahly on a permanent deal on 26 August, Michał Karbownik joining Olympiacos on a season-long loan on 27 August, Christian Walton signing with Ipswich Town on a season-long deal on 30 August (later joining them permanently on 19 January 2022), Andi Zeqiri moving to FC Augsburg on loan on 30 August, Moisés Caicedo joining Beerschot on a season-long loan on 31 August (recalled on 12 January 2022), Aaron Connolly joining Middlesbrough on loan on 2 January 2022, Jürgen Locadia joining VfL Bochum on a permanent deal on 5 January 2022, Taylor Richards joining Birmingham City on loan on 8 January 2022, Dan Burn signing with Newcastle United on a permanent deal on 31 January 2022, and Kjell Scherpen joining Oostende on loan on 31 January 2022.
